```suggestion

[param camera] is the [Camera3D] that the event originated in (for cameras inside viewports other than the main one to be detected, the parent [member Viewport.physics_object_picking] needs to be set to [code]true[/code]). ```

The first comma is just ungrammatical, which should be solved somehow. The second part is my suggestion to make it more readable, even though it's not formulated in a very technical way (which I think it doesn't have to be, as long as the meaning is clear).

The last part about `shape_idx` is technically correct but the meaning of the shape index remains a bit mysterious. In general `shape_find_owner(shape_idx)` can return a number that represents an abstract "shape owner" that can contain a number of internal (physics server) shapes, but in 99% of cases, when the shape comes from a standard node like `CollisionShape3D` or `CollisionPolygon3D`, you can do `shape_owner_get_owner(shape_find_owner(shape_idx))` to get the respective node. I'm not sure what's the best way to work this in, maybe just "see also `shape_find_owner` and `shape_owner_get_owner`". The same comment applies to the 2D case.

> event_position is the global position on the surface  resulted by  a raycast hit from the camera directed at the mouse

or just say
> event_position is the global position on the surface resulted by a raycast from the mouse and camera

body:
```suggestion
				Detects unhandled mouse and touch [InputEvent]s through [param event] when they happen while hovering over the object. Gesture events are not detected. [param camera] is the [Camera3D] that the event originated in (for cameras inside viewports other than the main one to be detected, the parent [member Viewport.physics_object_picking] needs to be set to [code]true[/code]). [param event_position] is the position hit by a raycast from the camera to the mouse, in global space. [param normal] is the normal vector of the surface at that point in world space. [param shape_idx] is the index of the detected shape from [PhysicsServer3D].
```
